races.name: Blink And You Miss It Sprint Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a soft-ground win on his card and an OR of 91; Kevin Stott retains the ride and the horse's best recent form has come at 5-6f on easier going, though 63 days off and a patchy recent string (-00819) ask questions of current sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, Solar Acclaim returns after 63 days and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid grounding for conditions; his ninth last time out tempers expectations, but at 136 lb from stall four, his overall profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Exclamation
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type with a strong win on good ground at this distance for Grace Harris; soft is unproven for this horse (all wins on good) and that going query is the key doubt, though OR 92 and a positive T14 record (5/15) give the yard confidence.
runners_data.comment: Exclamation has distance and going experience in his favour, and a second two starts back gives him a recent placed effort to build on; however, unplaced runs either side of that and a ranking of sixth of ten suggest he faces a stiff task under 135 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Cinque Verde
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field, and Beasley should enjoy an uncontested lead; his sole course-and-distance win came on good-to-firm and soft-ground form is limited (1/15 sim-going), so his ability to sustain the lead on today's surface is the critical question.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who steps back into 5f soft on a quick turnaround (8 days); his best recent effort was a fourth on soft over this trip, and David Nolan keeps the ride, though a low trainer strike rate (0/5 T14) and a moderate recent form string (099394) are both reasons for caution.
runners_data.comment: Sir Yoshi shaped with promise when third three starts back and returns here just eight days later in fine freshness, with experience over today's trip and going adding to his claims; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and a tough weight of 132 lb from stall eight may test his resolution.

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type with two wins on soft ground over 5f (including a course win), giving him a genuine going edge; PJ McDonald rides and hg:tp headgear is retained — the horse is a genuine player in any scenario where the front runners tire on the testing surface.
runners_data.comment: Trilby won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, but his last two outings have brought a defeat and a fourth, suggesting he may be just off the boil; 130 lb is no easy burden from stall three.

runners_data.name: Paddy's Day
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with sound recent placed form (357273) for Nigel Tinkler; course-and-distance experience is solid and the 3lb claim of Alex Jary (3) helps at the weights, though 57 days off and a lack of soft-ground wins in the history (no SOF in hist) are mild flags.
runners_data.comment: Paddy's Day arrives 57 days fresh and yet to win in his last six starts, though a third last time out and a second three starts back hint at ability; a trainer in poor current form — zero from 21 over the past fortnight — is the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Temple Of Athena
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type who has placed twice at this trip; Cam Hardie takes the ride and Brian Ellison's T14 figure (1/20) is modest — all recent runs have come on good or faster and soft ground is an unknown commodity for this three-year-old.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Temple Of Athena has been stuck in the minors in her last five starts, with a win six starts back her only recent bright spot, and a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight makes it hard to get enthusiastic despite experience over today's trip and distance.

runners_data.name: Francisco's Piece
runners_data.note: Won at this trip on good in his most recent start and has some soft-ground placed form; a natural hold-up horse whose true racing style means he is unlikely to get his preferred position in a race loaded with rear-runners, which compromises his chance significantly here.
runners_data.comment: Francisco's Piece arrives here in form, winning last time out and earning a rating of 90 that marks him out as one to beat from stall nine, carrying 128 lb; the chief concern is whether he can back that up after a 29-day absence.

runners_data.name: Lethal Nymph
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran of seven who has placed on soft before (2nd on GOO at 5f) and won on standard; Jason Hart takes the ride, but with Paul Midgley's T14 figure modest (2/13), getting into the race from the back in a compressed pace scenario is the tactical hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lethal Nymph is hard to fancy despite an encouraging win last time out; he has experience of today's trip and going, but his overall recent form is patchy and he represents a stiff ask from this position in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Soft-ground proven (3rd and 2nd on SOF at 5f) and Richard & Fahey yard in solid T14 form (5/47); races from the back naturally but, in a field crowded with hold-up types, will find it difficult to operate from his ideal position — the style-fit discount is real and tempers an otherwise interesting profile.
runners_data.comment: Vintage Clarets catches the eye on our rating, topping the field of ten, and he arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround with experience over today's trip and going, carrying 127 lb from stall two; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, though a third three starts back hints at residual ability.

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight with a preference for 6f and good ground (all hist runs at 6f or on good/standard); headgear (b) retained for Michael Appleby, but a natural hold-up horse unable to get his usual pitch, soft ground untested, and a step back to 5f all stack against him here.
runners_data.comment: Baldomero is winless in his last six starts and ranks ninth of ten on our figures, making him hard to fancy here; a third three starts back offers slim encouragement, but back-to-back disappointing runs since leave him with plenty to prove carrying 126 lb from stall 11.

races.paceDynamic: Cinque Verde is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Connor Beasley should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo — particularly significant on soft ground at Beverley's sharp 5f, where there is little room to make up ground and position from the outset matters enormously. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which compresses the field and limits the advantage available to hold-up types attempting to close from the rear. Solar Aclaim, Exclamation, Paddy's Day, and Temple Of Athena will push for prominent positions behind the leader, creating a bunched early order that will test those who get shuffled back. Francisco's Piece, Vintage Clarets, and Baldomero are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are more rear-runners in this field than can realistically operate from their natural position — in practice, at least some will find themselves further back than ideal. This race shape strongly favours horses who can secure a prominent pitch close to Cinque Verde, as a controlled single-leader tempo on soft ground is unlikely to set up a late finish for genuine hold-up types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cinque Verde Leads, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cinque Verde dictates a measured pace and the prominent horses track closely enough to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Beasley settles Cinque Verde into an uncontested rhythm on the soft, and horses like Solar Aclaim or Exclamation — travelling prominently throughout — have enough gas to collar or pass the leader late. Soft ground tests stamina evenly, and those who have been racing close to the pace all the way avoid the energy cost of a wide or tardy move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely moderate and Cinque Verde is never seriously pressed, allowing him to coast home.
scenarios.body: An uncontested lead on soft ground with a field of hold-up types behind is a genuine scenario for Cinque Verde to win travelling within himself, hitting the rising ground near the finish with energy in reserve. His sole win at this course and distance on similar ground is a key data point, and a lack of true pace pressure makes this shape real.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and horses with soft-ground stamina and a late run find the winner coming back to them.
scenarios.body: Trilby is the most credible beneficiary here, having won on soft ground over this trip and capable of producing a strong late surge if the front runners tire; Sir Yoshi and Lethal Nymph could also pick up ground if the race unfolds at a stronger tempo than expected. However, the redistribution of Francisco's Piece, Vintage Clarets, and Baldomero — all natural hold-up horses — means many of the true closers will be racing out of their best role and their chances are tempered accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Early, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for the prominent positions disrupts the predicted order and a horse from midfield slips through on the rail.
scenarios.body: With Solar Aclaim, Exclamation, Paddy's Day, and Temple Of Athena all seeking prominent ground behind the one confirmed leader, a scrappy opening furlong could see gaps appear; a horse like Trilby or Lethal Nymph finding a clean route through on the inside could capitalise. This scenario requires a degree of fortune and a specific rail bias to materialise, making it genuinely low-probability.

watchPoints.text: Cinque Verde's ability to sustain his lead on soft ground is pivotal — if he finds the testing surface beyond him in the closing stages, the race opens up dramatically for the prominent horses tracking him.

Solar Aclaim and Exclamation are both seeking prominent positions behind the sole front-runner — watch the first furlong for any bump or interference between these two that could compromise one or both.
Trilby's soft-ground form and course win make him a latent threat in any scenario where the pace collapses; if PJ McDonald can find a clean passage on the inner, he could arrive late and fast.

Francisco's Piece, Vintage Clarets, and Baldomero are all natural hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves further back than ideal — monitor their early positioning; if any manages to secure an unexpectedly prominent spot, its chance improves materially.

The Beverley 5f rising finish can expose horses who have used too much energy in the early stages on soft — watch for any prominent racer who hits the front too soon and ties up in the final 100 yards.

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Hull Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: L'Eagle Aid
runners_data.note: Has solid recent Goodwood form over 12f on good ground for Charlie Johnston, but the step to soft going here is untested and, as a genuine hold-up horse, he is competing for the same late-race turf as several others pushed toward the rear — temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placer who has finished third three times in his last four starts, L'Eagle Aid arrives fresh on 27 days' rest, has run over today's trip, and our rating puts him ahead of his official mark — yet to win in recent starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in the race, with two wins at Stamford Bridge and course experience at Beverley; has had 63 days off but returns to conditions he handles, and if allowed a soft lead here he is a live contender to follow up his OR 71 mark.
runners_data.comment: Clansman boasts a winner two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with his rating of 76 giving him a solid claims; the chief concern is that unplaced effort last time out after a 63-day break that stretches into this return.

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old mare who won over 11f on good at Goodwood and placed twice over 16f; she is a natural hold-up type squeezed toward the middle of the field by the volume of closers, so her ability to get a clear run from off the pace is central to her chance.
runners_data.comment: Valley of Flowers has won in recent starts but sits eighth of nine on our figures, making her hard to fancy at the weights with 137 lb to carry; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a run 36 days ago leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Prince Of Calypso
runners_data.note: A lightly raced 3-year-old for Edward Bethell who won over 12f at Stamford Bridge last time and handles soft (placed at Southwell); has gone headgear-less and is the most likely horse to press Clansman from a prominent pitch with a fresh Oisin Orr in the saddle on a progressive profile.
runners_data.comment: Prince Of Calypso won last time out and returns just 12 days later in fine fettle, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour; a rating of 78 underlines his claims, and he is our pick to go in again.

runners_data.name: Mayaada
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster 3-year-old with limited soft-ground exposure (2 runs) and a career best over 10f; stepping to 14f for the first time is a significant query and, as a true hold-up horse, she needs a strong pace that Clansman is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Mayaada shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip, while her rating of 79 makes her the one to beat here; the concern is a fourth last time out after 49 days off.

runners_data.name: Northern Brave
runners_data.note: Michael Dods 3-year-old who won over 8f on heavy and placed over 12f on good; a natural hold-up type who, given the lack of front-runners, is likely to push forward in running and race more prominently than the map suggests — watch for Connor Beasley settling him handy rather than at the rear.
runners_data.comment: Northern Brave shaped well last time, finishing second, though a fourth two starts back and a seventh three starts back hint at inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and returns after 28 days, carrying 132 lb on an official mark of 74.

runners_data.name: Unchartedterritory
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 3-year-old won over 9f on soft and placed on good ground, showing he handles cut; a hold-up horse likely to sit mid-to-prominent in this race shape, and his soft-ground win gives him a meaningful going edge over several rivals.
runners_data.comment: Unchartedterritory was a winner two starts back but ran flat last time, and that sixth leaves him needing to bounce back here; no distance or going experience is noted, though he arrives on a reasonable freshener of 21 days and our rating gives him a fighting chance in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Barak Warrior
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes the ride on this James Keane-trained 3-year-old who won over 12f on firm at Leicester last time; soft ground here is a genuine query given his best form on faster surfaces, and as a natural hold-up type he is competing for restricted late-race room.
runners_data.comment: Barak Warrior's recent form is patchy, with two sevenths and an eighth in his last five starts offsetting that win two starts back, and our figures rank him seventh of nine here, making him hard to fancy despite the distance experience and a third last time out.

runners_data.name: Topathemorning
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams 3-year-old with modest recent form (5th-8th) over shorter trips and no proven soft-ground form; the step up to 14f is uncharted, and as a hold-up type mapped centrally because of the volume of closers, he faces the stiffest ask of any runner in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with back-to-back eighths making her hard to fancy from the bottom of our rankings, Topathemorning at least returns reasonably fresh on 33 days off and carries a workable 120lb.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the off over 1m4f on soft ground at Beverley, he is likely to control this race at a sustainable, measured tempo from the front. Behind him, the bulk of the field are true hold-up types — L'Eagle Aid, Valley Of Flowers, Northern Brave, Barak Warrior and Topathemorning all prefer to race from off the pace — meaning the midfield will be congested and the genuine rear-of-field positions fewer than the race shape map can accommodate. Prince Of Calypso, Mayaada and Unchartedterritory are the most credible pressurisers from a prominent or mid-division pitch, but none is a natural front-runner capable of forcing Clansman into an honest gallop. The field holds more hold-up horses than can realistically secure their natural position; of the redistributed types, Northern Brave and Unchartedterritory look most likely to press forward and grab a more prominent pitch than their natural style suggests, given the absence of pace competition. A single-pace, steadily-run soft-ground affair over a stiff 1m4f favours those who can race prominently and quicken from a handy position, rather than deep closers who will be waiting on a late surge that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clansman Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman gets a soft lead and sets a fair but not gruelling tempo on soft ground, allowing a handy tracker to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Clansman dictates from the front on his favoured Beverley track, and the race is set up perfectly for any horse sitting second or third and travelling within themselves; soft ground over 1m4f on this stiff course places a premium on stamina and a smooth, prominent run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Clansman Leads And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman sets an uncontested lead at a pace perfectly suited to himself and none of the hold-up brigade can close on the strong Beverley straight.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied and an experienced front-runner in control, Clansman simply conserves energy throughout and has enough in reserve to repel challengers; his two wins at Stamford Bridge show course form is transferable and his last two runs at Beverley on this course suggest he is well placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman sets a stop-start crawl that brings the entire field into contention turning for home, compressing the race into a sprint-finish on soft ground.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race on soft ground could produce a bunched finish where stamina reserves and a clear run matter most; this shape marginally helps the redistributed hold-up horses if they can find daylight, though their out-of-role positioning makes a clean passage unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground proves significantly more demanding than anticipated and the pace collapses in the home straight, turning the race into a stamina slog.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven soft-ground form and the biggest stamina reserves will grind past a tiring field; this is the least likely shape given Clansman's experienced front-running profile.

watchPoints.text: Clansman is uncontested up front — watch whether Billy Garritty attempts to steal this on the front end given the complete absence of pace pressure; if he builds a significant advantage, closers will struggle to reel him in on soft ground over 1m4f.

Prince Of Calypso is the most likely horse to track Clansman and dictate the terms for the prominent challengers — watch his early positioning; if Oisin Orr slots in second, he controls the narrative for the rest of the race.

Northern Brave and Unchartedterritory are both natural hold-up horses likely to push forward in this race due to the absence of pace — watch for a contested midfield scramble for position in the first two furlongs that may unsettle some of the more reluctant stayers.

Valley Of Flowers, L'Eagle Aid and Barak Warrior are all true hold-up types competing for the same late-race ground; if the field stacks up in the straight, a traffic-jam finish becomes a real risk and the horse with the cleanest passage, not necessarily the best form, may benefit.

Soft ground is confirmed across the card at Beverley today — watch the market for any drifters among runners whose recent form is exclusively on good or faster, particularly Barak Warrior (firm win last time) and Mayaada (all form on good).

races.name: Dearing Plastics Celebrating 40 Years Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: Won twice at 10f on good ground recently but soft-ground record is stark (0W0P from 15 similar-going runs), and at 1m2f — two furlongs longer than those soft-ground efforts — stamina in testing conditions is unproven; genuine hold-up operator who needs a strong pace to deliver.
runners_data.comment: Shimmering Sands won back-to-back races earlier in this sequence and ran third last time out to advertise solid current form, and with distance experience and a 22-day break leaving him fresh, the main query is whether 142 lb will anchor his chance from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Project Geofin
runners_data.note: P J McDonald takes over on a five-year-old who finished third over 10f on good ground last time, but has never won or placed in similar soft going (0W0P from 15 runs) and drops into this 1m2f contest without soft-ground credentials to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a second five starts back, Project Geofin returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having run over today's trip before, and his rating of 82 marks him as the one to beat from stall 11 off 142 lb, though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here — recent form of 1-2 at 10f on good ground is solid and Jessica Macey's yard has one winner from six in the last 14 days; the STYLE_FIT flag notes it is technically racing out of its optimal prominent role by being pushed onto the lead, but in practice that front position is exactly where it will find itself and the soft ground suits a controlling front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a placed effort three starts back, bringing solid recent form and distance experience to the table; the risk is that a fourth last time out shows he does not always fire, and 142 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr rides a three-year-old carrying only 133lbs who has won three of its last four at 10f on good ground; soft-going form is limited (0W0P from 11 runs) but a prominent racing style means it will track Everyoneknowsadave naturally and is well-placed to pounce if the leader tires.
runners_data.comment: Ciao Capo won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, giving him solid claims, though a sixth two starts back interrupts the sequence and 133 lb is no featherweight ask from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Rapide Vega
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 8f on a sound surface and placed twice at 10f on good ground — most importantly, picked up one placing from seven soft-ground appearances, making it the most soft-ground-credentialled of the prominent trio; M P Sheehy keeps it simple from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Rapide Vega won last time out and returns fit on just 12 days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going; at 133 lb from stall one, the weight is the one factor worth watching.

runners_data.name: Musical Accord
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old returns after 86 days off with a limited three-run form string (all sixth or seventh), holds a genuine hold-up profile and has never tackled ground as testing as today; the extended absence and lack of soft form make this a watch-and-learn run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Musical Accord faces a stiff ask returning from 86 days off, though she has run over today's trip and a spot of freshness can occasionally spark improvement.

runners_data.name: Ziata
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a three-year-old who won over 10f on good ground and has placed twice in soft going (0W1P from seven); true prominent racer who should find a workable position just behind the front pair, though the field's traffic means it may be squeezed for room.
runners_data.comment: Ziata showed she can win, landing the spoils two starts back, though she comes here on the back of an unplaced effort and faces a stiff task ranked sixth of eleven; she has run over today's trip and going, and 129 lb from stall four is the reality she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old won twice on soft ground in 2024 at 9-10f — the soft form is genuine — but as a natural prominent type pushed into a midfield position by field congestion (REDISTRIBUTED), it races below its ideal tactical pitch today and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Fans Favourite arrives here on the back of a third last time out, and a winner three starts back, giving him a mixed profile to weigh up; experience over today's trip and going helps, though carrying 128 lb from stall six on a our rating of 73 makes this no gimme.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent six-year-old has placed 14 times in 15 soft-ground runs (0W1P) but is a true hold-up type displaced into a midfield slot because the rear is overcrowded; racing against its natural grain and without the strong gallop it needs to deploy its finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Sunny Orange ranks tenth of eleven on our figures and looks hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a fresh 14-day break carrying 126 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Distinction
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran whose soft-going record shows 1W2P from 15 visits — the experience is there — but Billy Garritty inherits a horse wearing a visor that is a genuine hold-up specialist bumped forward on the map; without a truly strong pace, its late effort is likely to fall short.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with just one placed effort in that sequence, Distinction is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before; the 23-day break offers little consolation.

runners_data.name: Lady Hornblower
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's three-year-old is naturally a prominent racer but is mapped to midfield because the pace positions are full; that demotion, combined with a soft-ground record of 0W1P from nine runs and a tendency to underperform on testing ground, makes today a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Hornblower at least showed some promise with a third two runs back, though her most recent seventh suggests she remains inconsistent; she has run over today's distance and going before, but a mark of 62 and draw two leave her with plenty to find under 122 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Everyoneknowsadave is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, will likely dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on soft ground over 1m2f at Beverley — a track that already rewards those who travel well through a race. That uncontested lead on a testing surface is a significant tactical advantage, allowing Everyoneknowsadave to control fractions and preserve energy into the final climb. Behind, Ciao Capo and Rapide Vega are the other genuine prominent types likely to slot into second and third early, while Lady Hornblower and Fans Favourite — both true prominent racers — are competing for positions the map cannot accommodate and will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently without burning resources, as the soft ground will drain stamina from hold-up runners who need a strong pace to close into. The field contains more natural front-running and prominent types than the pace map can place — Fans Favourite and Lady Hornblower in particular are unlikely to secure their natural position and will race less effectively than their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Everyoneknowsadave Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave gets a clean break and controls a moderate tempo from the front with no sustained pressure.
scenarios.body: On soft ground over 1m2f at Beverley's testing uphill finish, a front-runner allowed to set its own rhythm conserves energy that hold-up horses must find late — Everyoneknowsadave's recent form (1-2 in last three) and Rhys Elliott's experience aboard make this the dominant shape. Horses able to travel in the slipstream — Ciao Capo and Rapide Vega — are best placed to mount the only credible challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ciao Capo or Rapide Vega track Everyoneknowsadave closely and overhaul it in the final two furlongs when the soft ground takes its toll on the leader.
scenarios.body: Both hold solid recent form at this trip — Ciao Capo has won three of its last four at 10f on good ground and Rapide Vega grabbed a soft-ground win last time — and either could exploit a slightly generous pace set by Everyoneknowsadave on tiring ground. The prominent positions they secure naturally make them the most logical beneficiaries when the front-runner begins to flatten out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough through the middle section to string the field out and create a true stamina test that rewards the deepest stayer.
scenarios.body: Shimmering Sands and Project Geofin are genuine hold-up operators who have shown ability at 10f on good ground, but neither carries compelling soft-ground credentials (both 0W0P in similar going) and a solo front-runner is unlikely to generate the true pace they need. Sunny Orange and Distinction are redistributed from their natural hold-up positions and are racing out of role, reducing the probability of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave is challenged early by one of the displaced prominent types bidding to reclaim a front position, causing an unsustainably fast early tempo that burns all pace.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely scenario, the field implodes in the final two furlongs and a midfield or rear-of-field runner with stamina catches the spent leaders on the soft surface. Musical Accord, lightly raced and off 86 days, is an unknown quantity that could theoretically emerge if conditions suit an untested staying profile.

watchPoints.text: Everyoneknowsadave dominates the pace map as the sole front-runner — if it breaks cleanly and settles, it could control this entire race from flag to finish on soft ground.

Fans Favourite and Lady Hornblower are both natural prominent types who cannot both get the position they want — monitor the early stages for one or both being checked or forced wider, compromising their race entirely.
Ciao Capo's weight of only 133lbs as a three-year-old against older rivals could prove decisive late on soft ground — watch whether Oisin Orr tracks the leader from the second position.
Sunny Orange has placed in 14 of 15 soft-ground starts but is racing out of its natural hold-up position today — if the pace is modest, its finishing run will be blunted before it can be deployed.

Musical Accord returning after 86 days for Ralph Beckett on soft ground with a bare three-run form string is an unknown variable — if freshness translates to improvement, it could outrun its unfancied position.

races.name: IRE-Incentive, It Pays To Buy Irish EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Churchill Tyres Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with David Nolan aboard; best recent soft-ground form reads 6th of 15 in similar conditions, and a return to soft suits in theory, but Beverley's uphill finish asks for sustained galloping rather than a late sprint and the six-day turnaround from a seventh at Beverley is modest prep.
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround in fine fettle, his rating of 85 suggesting he merits more respect than his official mark of 78 implies; the concern is that he has been winless in his last six starts, and breaking that duck from stall one is the challenge.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride on this in-form four-year-old who has won twice and placed at 8f on good — the drop to 7½f on soft is the key question, with her one soft-ground run producing a 6th at 8f; three recent wins suggest confidence is high and prominent racing style should give her every chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, The Sweet Escape makes this a tough assignment despite a lively recent sequence of three wins in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and returns on a sound 15-day break, but the weight of 136 lb from stall 13 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Swift Salian
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who goes well on soft (1W, 3P in 7 soft runs) and clearly relishes forcing the pace; the task here is whether duelling with Mudamer on a soft Beverley track burns too much energy before the climb, though William Pyle keeps the ride and five recent placings show consistency.
runners_data.comment: Swift Salian has been a model of consistency in placing, with three seconds in his last five starts, though he remains yet to win and an unplaced run last time out is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough to threaten again.

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides this hold-up type who won on soft at 8f earlier this season; the step back to 7½f may just about suit and his soft-ground record is solid, but he has been beaten in 17 runners fields before and needs a genuinely strong pace to deliver his late run.
runners_data.comment: Zowal has a win three starts back and was third two starts back, but an unplaced effort last time and a ranking of tenth of twelve on our figures make him hard to fancy; he has run over today's trip and 35 days off shouldn't inconvenience him.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing six-year-old for Connor Beasley and Michael Dods who has won at 8f on good recently but has no soft-ground form in his last five — the going is a concern, though he handles Beverley-style tracks and his 1W, 1P from five good-ground runs on similar courses suggests class to be competitive.
runners_data.comment: Glenfinnan won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but an unplaced effort two starts back and 142 lb from stall 10 are factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Obelix
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading in the finish; Paul Mulrennan takes over but all five recent runs are on good ground and his tendency to drop away late on a track that demands a genuine galloping finish is a structural worry in soft conditions.

runners_data.name: Mudamer
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner in this contest, and at 45 days since last seen he is fresh enough to run his race; soft-going experience is limited (1W, 1P from two soft runs) and the seven-year-old has been running consistently around good ground — Oisin McSweeney takes the ride and whether he can cross to Salian early is the key tactical question.
runners_data.comment: Mudamer has placed three times in his last five starts, including third last time out, and has run over today's distance and going before, making him a genuine threat from stall two on a mark of 80; the concern is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: David Allan and Tim Easterby send out this five-year-old who has placed at 7f on soft and travels prominently; Tim Easterby's operation is in strong form (5 from 86 in 14 days) and Son's recent second at 7f soft is directly relevant form — he is perhaps the most straightforward fit for the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out on suitable distance and going, Son heads this 12-runner field as the top-rated contender on an 87 rating, and a return to form after a flat run two starts back looks on the cards; yet to win in recent starts, he nevertheless appeals as the one to beat under 139 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: One Night Thunder
runners_data.note: Conor Whiteley (5lb claim) takes the ride; a hold-up type whose best recent effort was a 3rd at 7f on good and whose soft-ground record shows 1W, 2P from four runs — the claim helps on the figures but a 22-day break and a form string of -03876 does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, One Night Thunder does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return to form showed with a third four starts back; however, recent efforts of sixth, seventh and eighth suggest he faces a stiff task from stall four carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Arduis Invicta
runners_data.note: Three-year-old running for Craig Lidster who has been placed at 5f and 6f on good; this is a step up to 7½f on soft, which is both a distance and a going question for a horse whose entire recent record is on good ground — Tom Eaves is a strong booking but the profile is unproven at this trip and in these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Arduis Invicta nonetheless shaped with promise when second three starts back, and our rating of 86 marks her as a serious contender here; the risk is that unplaced efforts last time out and six starts back raise a question over consistency.

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer with Kevin Stott up for Julie Camacho; has placed twice on similar-style good-ground tracks and a run of 3-1-4-3-4 shows consistency — the soft going is untested and 51 days off the track adds a fitness query, but the headgear note (h) and place record at 7f suggest he is not without a chance.
runners_data.comment: Highland Shah returns after 51 days off and, ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, is hard to fancy at these weights, though he does bring a win two starts back and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Shadow Run
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's three-year-old is a natural hold-up horse who has been pushed into a midfield map position because the field's true hold-up contingent is too large for the rear slots — his soft-going form reads 0W, 1P from five runs and Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is the booking angle, though racing out of his preferred position tempers the assessment.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Run has shown consistency without converting, with a second two starts back and fifth last time out, but he remains winless in recent starts and his trainer is in a difficult patch of form at just 4% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr partners this three-year-old who arrives with a recent win and two runner-up finishes, a pattern of form that is eye-catching; however, as a genuine hold-up type redistributed into a midfield position on the map because of race shape congestion, he is unlikely to get as far back as he ideally wants — Richard and Peter Fahey's yard has strong recent numbers and the 7f trip on soft is within range.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Supreme Clarets faces a stiff ask, though he arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving connections something to build on.

races.paceDynamic: Mudamer and Swift Salian are the two confirmed front-runners in this 13-runner field, and with both likely to press for early supremacy on soft ground over 7½f at Beverley, an honest-to-contested gallop is the baseline expectation — neither is the type to simply surrender and tuck in. That sustained tempo on a soft Beverley track, which climbs through the home straight and punishes those who race keenly up front, sets up the race for horses who travel smoothly in the first half and pick up off the pace. The field holds more prominent/hold-up types than the map can accommodate: Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed into midfield positions on the map because there is no room for them at their natural rear pitch — The Sweet Escape, Son, Glenfinnan, and Arduis Invicta all press for the prominent positions and some must drop back from their preferred spots. On balance, this race shape most strongly favours the genuine mid-to-prominent racer who settles comfortably behind the duelling front pair, avoids the soft-ground traffic battle on the rail, and produces a sustained run from two out — patient hold-up horses with a late burst are disadvantaged by Beverley's uphill finish which rewards galloping relentlessness over a single sharp kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Crew
scenarios.trigger: If Mudamer and Swift Salian fight for the lead, burning energy on soft ground and setting up a strong-run race throughout.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off through the first half, leaving the prominent horses travelling in behind to mow them down in the final two furlongs as the leaders tie up on the climb. Horses who settled just off the early battle in the first three or four positions are in the prime slot to swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Finds Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners establishes a clear lead without a sustained duel and the pace steadies.
scenarios.body: A more measured tempo gives the leader(s) a chance to control the race and ration their effort, making them harder to pass in the straight on soft ground. Front-running types and horses with tactical speed to land in the first two positions become the main dangers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly severe and the front pair cut each other's throats, leaving a gap for the closers.
scenarios.body: A burning tempo and tired leaders would theoretically open the door for genuine rear-runners, but Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets — the truest hold-up horses — have been crowded out of their natural positions, reducing the likelihood they get far enough back to produce their best run. Misunderstood and Zowal, both held up on soft-ground form, remain the best candidates if a late surge is on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is moderate and the field bunches, turning the race into a stamina test from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A muddling gallop on soft ground at Beverley that reignites briefly in the straight can catch out the midfield and hold-up brigade who need the race to be truly run, instead rewarding a horse with tactical pace and clean air. Glenfinnan, who has course form and travels prominently, and Son, who handles soft and sits handy, profile best for this unpredictable scenario.

watchPoints.text: Mudamer and Swift Salian are both genuine front-runners drawn in a 13-runner soft-ground field — watch whether either blinks at the start or one crosses the other in the first furlong, because the horse who wins that duel dictates the entire tempo of the race.

Shadow Run and Supreme Clarets are true hold-up horses who cannot get to the back of the field as they would want — if either is caught in traffic mid-race on soft ground without their natural run through, their chance is effectively over before the home turn.

The Sweet Escape has winning form at 8f on good but this is 7½f on soft — watch the market move carefully, as Joanna Mason will have to commit earlier than this horse's recent form suggests, and if she cannot travel prominently she may not get home.

Obelix is flagged for fading in the finish; in soft ground on a track that demands stamina up the Beverley hill, any sign of him disputing a prominent pitch in the early stages should be noted as a negative — he is most dangerous when covered up quietly and produced late, which the race shape may not allow.

Glenfinnan's soft-ground record is genuinely absent across his last five runs — all five are on good — and while Connor Beasley knows the track, watch for any signs of him struggling to pick up off the bridle once the climb begins, which would confirm the going as a concern for his win chance.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week 2026 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner for Michael & David Easterby, Joanna Mason takes over; soft form reads 5/15 with no wins, and stepping up from 7f-8f trips in recent starts makes this 1m½f an unknown stamina test — likely to press hard early at personal cost.
runners_data.comment: Glorious Kitty landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and a runner-up finish two starts back underlines her consistency at this level; the main concern is that sixth last time out leaves her needing to bounce back after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran for Sam England with headgear (tongue-piece), prominent style suits a genuine pace in this field; best soft-ground form is 1W1P from just two runs, and a 34-day break is not a major concern at this age given his consistency.
runners_data.comment: Coolree has shown some ability — third two starts back and runner-up on a couple of occasions in recent starts — yet has gone winless in his last six, and a seventh last time out after 34 days raises a fitness query; he has distance and going experience to call on, but looks to have it all to do from eighth in the draw.

runners_data.name: Borjina
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Edward Bethell (in fine T14 form: 7/29), Kevin Stott takes the ride; all recent starts on Good to Firm or standard ground make the soft surface the key unknown, though the step up to 1m½f from 7f-8f trips looks a natural progression.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 10 of 12 on our figures, Borjina is hard to fancy at the weights, though she does return from a 31-day break in reasonable order and has run over today's trip before; a second two starts back is her only recent encouragement, with a fifth last time out and a seventh three starts back making the overall profile uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old for David O'Meara, Conor Whiteley claims 5lb; soft-ground record reads 0W0P from one run, and all five recent starts came on Good — going is a genuine question mark, though the form string shows consistent placing at this level.
runners_data.comment: Placed in three of her last four starts, including a second two runs back and third last time out, Sandy Craic arrives here in fine recent nick after 21 days off and has run over today's trip before; the main risk is whether her rating of 71 can quite match the demands at the top of the weights carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Good Morning Alex
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from a 101-day absence for David & Nicola Barron, William Pyle takes the ride; carries top weight of 141lbs and recent form (670850) is uninspiring, but boasts 1W2P from five soft-ground runs suggesting the conditions at least don't inconvenience.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 101 days off, Good Morning Alex faces questions about fitness, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a fifth two starts back offers a modest crumb of encouragement from an otherwise disappointing recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Regalian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood, back just 7 days after his last run with a headgear change to a plain nose-band from the previous hood; form reads six consecutive placed or worse finishes and soft-ground figures (0W0P) add little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Regalian is winless in his last five starts but rates well clear of his rivals on our figures, and with experience over today's trip and going already banked, he arrives fit just seven days on from his latest outing carrying 140 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Style Of Life
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with tongue-tie and tongue-plate, Tom Kiely-Marshall claims 5lb; recent form (125-00) shows a sharp decline after a win 15 days ago and back-to-back zeros are concerning — must lead and dictate but faces direct company from Glorious Kitty who will fight for the same position.

runners_data.name: Glen Nevis
runners_data.note: Prominent-style three-year-old for Charlie Johnston (T14: 5/39), Jason Hart up; all five recent runs on Good ground and the soft surface is an untested factor, though the step up to 1m½f from 8f looks potentially positive given a pedigree that should get the trip.
runners_data.comment: Glen Nevis has been remarkably consistent in recent starts, finishing second twice and third once in his last six, and returning fresh on just nine days' rest having run over today's trip before; the risk is he remains yet to win in that same sequence.

runners_data.name: Tarmonbarry Kid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Richard & Peter Fahey (T14: 5/47), Oisin Orr takes over; returned a winner on Soft last time on form and 1W1P from six soft-ground runs makes him one of the stronger pace-scenario beneficiaries if the front-runners tire — 73 days off is the only minor flag.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Tarmonbarry Kid brings solid recent form to the table, though 73 days off the track is a query and his speed figure of 64 leaves him with ground to make up from stall 12 off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: A genuine back-of-field type in practice, Tim Easterby's six-year-old carries a tongue-tie and boot combination and has won off a higher OR; pushed into a midfield map position because the hold-up slots are oversubscribed, meaning he may not get his preferred unhurried run, which tempers enthusiasm for his late-race threat.
runners_data.comment: Mount King has shown little consistency in recent starts, with a ninth and a fourth from his last two outings overshadowing a win four starts back, and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures he is hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Prominent-style five-year-old for Ruth Carr, James Sullivan rides; recent form (113744) includes back-to-back wins before tailing off, with 1W2P on soft across the dataset — the step up to 1m½f from a career spent at 7f is the significant unknown and could find her outstayed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Filey Beach has posted two fourths in his most recent starts and a seventh three runs back, making him hard to fancy despite a win two starts further back; experience over today's trip and going, plus 22 days' freshness, are modest plus points.

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse in normal circumstances for John Mackie, P J McDonald takes the ride; the map places him in midfield because genuine hold-up berths are at a premium with this many finishers-from-rear in the field — if he cannot drop in and settle, his finishing kick is likely blunted on soft ground over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Cobalt Comet faces a stiff task, and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's trip and going before and did score one start back.

races.paceDynamic: Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty are the two confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner field, and both are expected to press for the lead from the off on soft ground over 1m½f at Beverley — a combination that almost certainly produces a genuinely contested, honest gallop rather than a crawl. Style Of Life (Tom Kiely-Marshall, tongue-tie, tongue-plate) and Glorious Kitty (Joanna Mason) will fight for supremacy early, ensuring the pace is true and the ground will take its toll on horses who burn energy in the vanguard. The field carries more pace than can naturally be accommodated — Mount King and Cobalt Comet are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear is crowded with their type, meaning their true role cannot be secured in this shape. This race shape — a genuine two-horse battle up front on soft ground — strongly favours patient, well-positioned hold-up or late-midfield runners who can sit off the contested pace and pick up the pieces in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty burn each other out early and the race falls apart up front in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine gallop on soft ground, tire badly in the closing stages, and horses held up off the pace arrive to mop up; soft ground amplifies the stamina test and makes this the most likely outcome in a genuine two-horse lead battle over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Sit, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a strong pace but one prominent runner is able to track close enough to pounce without getting caught in the early scrimmage.
scenarios.body: A horse like Sandy Craic or Glen Nevis sits just off the pace in second or third, conserves energy through the middle stages, and hits the front with enough momentum to hold on as the true closers are too far back to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Style Of Life with the tongue-tie tactical advantage) disengages from the duel and steals a march turning for home.
scenarios.body: Style Of Life has won off a similar OR at this track before and, if Glorious Kitty fades having pressed too hard, the remaining leader can exploit a soft-ground slog at honest but not suicidal pace; the field may be too strung out to reel them in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Hold-Ups Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel fractures chaotically and the closers get an uncharacteristically clean passage on the wide Beverley straight.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Cobalt Comet and Mount King — both redistributed away from their natural hold-up roles — actually securing the back-of-field position they prefer, which is improbable in this congested setup; even if it occurs, soft ground over 1m½f leaves little room to make up ground from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Style Of Life and Glorious Kitty — watch the first two furlongs to see whether either horse gives way or whether they fight stride for stride; a prolonged battle between these two front-runners will inflate the pace dramatically and increase the chance of a closer dominating the finish.

Tarmonbarry Kid — Oisin Orr is a high-quality booking for the Fahey yard and this horse has a winning soft-ground run in the book; if he gets a clear passage from his hold-up position as the front-runners fade, he could arrive late with a strong challenge.

Borjina — Edward Bethell's T14 strike rate of 7/29 is the best in the race and Kevin Stott is a leading northern jockey; watch whether she settles in hold-up position on her first try at soft ground, as any unsettled behaviour will cost her dearly in the closing stages.

Mount King and Cobalt Comet — both are genuine hold-up horses drawn into a congested midfield on the map; watch early to see whether either can drop back to their natural position or whether they get shuffled into an unfavourable tracking role that neutralises their finishing effort.

Glen Nevis — Charlie Johnston's yard (5/39 T14) and Jason Hart is a strong combination; watch whether the step up to 1m½f on softening ground brings out improvement or whether he simply hasn't got the stamina to sustain a prominent effort over this trip.
